weaknesses: Essential ablations are missing. The paper does not report the claimed comparison with random/PCA splits, or controlled comparisons isolating tree partitioning, the improved leaf RFM, diagonal versus full AGOP, adaptive bandwidth, kernel choice, leaf size, and split-subsample size. Consequently, the source of the gains and the value of the main novelty are unclear.

The scalability and efficiency claims are overstated. Runtime plots use only the selected configuration and exclude hyperparameter-search cost; hardware, memory use, and resource matching are unspecified; empirical scaling is demonstrated principally on one dataset up to 350,000 samples; and the model still stores kernel centers for all training examples and evaluates against up to 60,000 centers per prediction. This does not support scaling to “essentially unlimited” data.

Several details needed for correctness and reproduction are absent or inconsistent: values for the split-model sample size and regularization, RFM iteration count and stability parameter, tuning budget, seeds, classification-label handling, and validation-refill procedure are missing. Moreover, C is described as both a maximum leaf size and a minimum split-subset size, the AGOP matrix exponent from the RFM definition disappears from the leaf algorithm, and the promised code URL is blank.

The stated balanced-split guarantee is false when projection values have ties, which are common for categorical or discrete tabular features. The specified median rule can create severely imbalanced or empty children, yet no tie-breaking or degenerate-split termination rule is given.

The interpretability evidence is qualitative and selectively illustrated. AGOP measures model sensitivity rather than causal or necessarily reliable feature importance; there is no quantitative feature-recovery, stability, fidelity, or comparison with SHAP/tree-based importance, and some domain conclusions go beyond what gradient outer products establish.

Evaluation reporting has notable reliability issues: uncertainty across splits is largely absent, the meta-test comparison imports results with unclear compute/tuning equivalence, and Table B.10 labeled as binary TabArena results exactly duplicates the regression Table B.8. The method is a relatively direct combination of an existing RFM with hierarchical local modeling, while positioning against prior local-kernel, mixture-of-experts, and supervised partitioning approaches is limited. Given the missing component analysis, the degree of novelty is difficult to establish.
